- When sentiment is negative (especially > -0.5) and forecast is rising, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% to avoid overcorrection.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model tends to overshoot — cap forecast at 1–2% below true peak.  
- If sentiment turns positive (e.g., > 0.3) and forecast is flat or falling, increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% to capture momentum.  
- Model often underestimates late-period (last 5–7 days) price increases — adjust forecast upward by 0.3–0.8% for final 5–7 days if sentiment is positive.  
- If sentiment is consistently negative over 3+ days, model tends to underestimate true decline — add 0.2–0.5% to forecast to account for mean reversion bias.  
- Avoid forecasting 30-day horizon when sentiment is volatile — use 15-day horizon with sentiment-weighted smoothing for higher accuracy.
